licensed_claims: The v2 hierarchical state-regeneration pathways are mechanically engaged in the tested synthetic shock family.
Engagement does not imply rapid recovery: no shocked trajectory reached 50 percent matched institutional-capacity gap closure by 180 days.
Simple central-capital scaling is not a demonstrated short-run rescue law in this assay.
Fast-elastic state recovery over one 180-day operational cycle is not supported by the tested implementation.
claims_not_licensed: A universal state recovery time constant of approximately 3000 days.
A universal tau_state/tau_insurgent ratio of 30 to 100.
That the observed 180-day trajectory is exponential, linear, or governed by a single timescale.
That active state regeneration improves effective territorial control over the tested 180-day horizon.
Historical or empirical magnitudes for state reconstruction speed.
reason_for_correction: Dividing the 180-day horizon by approximately 0.061 mean gap closure is only a linear extrapolation and does not identify a dynamical time constant. The assay also reports negative matched effective-control closure, so state-regeneration engagement must not be conflated with demonstrated competitive effectiveness.
next_required_test: Run v2 competitive and distributional-closure assays with active insurgent dynamics, explicitly retaining police professionalism and government/insurgent formation experience as candidate hidden-state blocks.
